related_questions.question: How long do COVID germs stay in the air?

text_blocks.snippet: COVID-19 virus particles can remain airborne for hours, potentially lingering in the air after an infected person has left the space. Studies suggest the virus can stay airborne for up to 3 hours. Factors like ventilation and room size can influence how long the virus remains airborne according to the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (.gov).

list.title: Airborne Transmission:
list.snippet: COVID-19 can be spread through the air via small droplets and particles, which can linger in the air for extended periods.

list.title: Duration:
list.snippet: Research indicates that the virus can remain viable in the air for up to 3 hours, according to WebMD.

list.title: Factors Affecting Duration:
list.snippet: Ventilation systems, room size, and the presence of air filtration systems can impact how long the virus stays airborne.

list.title: Persistence:
list.snippet: The virus can be present in the air even after an infected person has left the space.

text_blocks.snippet: If you've been exposed to COVID-19, immediately begin taking precautions. This includes wearing a high-quality mask or respirator, avoiding crowded places, and taking extra care around those at higher risk of severe illness. You should also test for COVID-19 at least 5 days after your exposure, even if you don't have symptoms.

list.title: Start Precautions Immediately:
list.snippet: Don't wait for symptoms to appear. Begin wearing a high-quality mask or respirator (like an N95) as soon as you know about the exposure.

list.title: Avoid Crowded Places:
list.snippet: Limit your exposure to crowded indoor settings where you can't wear a mask consistently.

list.title: Consider Your Risk Factors:
list.snippet: If you or those around you are at higher risk for severe illness, take extra precautions and consider consulting with a healthcare professional.

list.title: Test at Least 5 Days After Exposure:
list.snippet: Get tested for COVID-19, even if you don't have symptoms. Testing helps identify infection early.

list.title: Continue Precautions for 10 Days:
list.snippet: Even with a negative test, continue taking precautions for a full 10 days after your last exposure.
